title: Strongly Convex Sets in Riemannian Manifolds
claim: Several definitions of strong convexity are distinct yet related, each captured by a different geometric construction on the same curved space.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, tangent-plane mapping arrows in center and right
description: Three side-by-side panels each show an orange sphere representing a Riemannian manifold M. A subset C is shaded on it, with two points x and y joined by a dotted geodesic through a midpoint γ(t). The left panel shows a red geodesic ball around γ(t) that lies inside C, with the set-builder inequality written above it. The center panel adds a gray tangent plane T_xM and an arrow to a second plane, where the inverse exponential image of C appears as an orange ellipse containing a dashed circle. The right panel shows a tangent plane at γ(t) with a red disk of radius αt(1−t)d²(x,y) and an arrow labeled Exp_γ(t)(·) pointing back to the sphere. Red and orange dominate. The eye goes first to the glowing red regions on the spheres.

abstract: Strong convexity plays a key role in designing and analyzing convex optimization algorithms and is well-understood in Hilbert spaces. However, the notion of strongly convex sets beyond Hilbert spaces remains unclear. In this paper, we propose various definitions of strong convexity for uniquely geodesic sets in a Riemannian manifold, examine their relationships, introduce tools to identify geodesically strongly convex sets, and analyze the convergence of optimization algorithms over these sets. In particular, we show that the Riemannian Frank-Wolfe algorithm converges linearly when the Riemannian scaling inequalities hold.
